sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球排名前列的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这都是该大学促进所有生物生活质量这一使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 详情请访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the U.S., they're called lines.
sentences.zh: 在美国，它们被称为“lines”（排队）。

sentences.en: In Canada, apparently they're called lineups sometimes.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大，它们有时似乎被称为“lineups”。

sentences.en: And I was once interviewed live on Canadian national radio, and they started talking about lineups,
sentences.zh: 有一次我接受加拿大国家电台的直播采访，他们开始谈论“lineups”，

sentences.en: and we had a conversation about police for five minutes until I realized what they were talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了五分钟的警察，直到我意识到他们说的是排队。

sentences.en: But pretty much everywhere else, it's known as a Q.
sentences.zh: 但在几乎其他所有地方，它都被称为“Q”（队列）。

sentences.en: I like Q the beSt. Yeah, me too.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢“Q”这个词。我也是。

sentences.en: That's Benjamin Walker.
sentences.zh: 那是本杰明·沃克。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with Q's.
sentences.zh: 他痴迷于队列（Q's）。

sentences.en: He keeps sending me emails with links to YouTube videos of Q's.
sentences.zh: 他总是给我发邮件，附上关于队列的 YouTube 视频链接。

sentences.en: You have psychology students filming their surreptitious Q experiments.
sentences.zh: 你会看到心理学专业的学生拍摄他们偷偷进行的队列实验。

sentences.en: You have Asian road rage videos.
sentences.zh: 你会看到亚洲的路怒视频。

sentences.en: You've got people filming fights that break out in Q's.
sentences.zh: 你还会看到人们拍摄在队列中爆发的争吵。

sentences.en: Unless you're going to physically move me, nothing's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 除非你打算把我物理挪走，否则什么都不会发生。

sentences.en: So understand that I'm not getting out of this line.
sentences.zh: 所以请明白，我是不会离开这个队列的。

sentences.en: And understand that none of you are going to stop me from being innocent.
sentences.zh: 也请明白，你们谁也别想阻止我保持清白。

sentences.en: I like to call YouTube the Q-hole.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把 YouTube 称为“Q-hole”（队列黑洞）。

sentences.en: And when I found this lecture by Dr. Q, I immediately made an appointment to go and see him.
sentences.zh: 当我发现 Q 博士的这个讲座时，我立刻预约去见他。

sentences.en: I'm Dick Larson.
sentences.zh: 我是迪克·拉尔森。

sentences.en: I'm a professor at MIT.
sentences.zh: 我是麻省理工学院的教授。

sentences.en: And I guess my nickname is Dr. Q.
sentences.zh: 我想我的绰号是 Q 博士。

sentences.en: Dick Larson is a Q theoriSt.
sentences.zh: 迪克·拉尔森是一位队列理论家。

sentences.en: Just about every day, we experience Q-ing in some aspect of our lives.
sentences.zh: 几乎每天，我们生活的方方面面都会经历排队。

sentences.en: Dick Larson studies the mathematical and psychological models of Q-ing systeMs.
sentences.zh: 迪克·拉尔森研究队列系统的数学和心理模型。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, oftentimes too many Q's on a day-to-day basis.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，日常生活中往往有太多的队列。

sentences.en: Dr. Q is able to put his professional knowledge to work everywhere he goes.
sentences.zh: Q 博士无论走到哪里，都能运用他的专业知识。

sentences.en: I have my own ways through supermarkets, particularly if you have to go to the deli counter and get a number.
sentences.zh: 我在超市里有自己的一套方法，特别是如果你必须去熟食柜台取号的话。

sentences.en: You run to the deli counter as soon as you go into the supermarket, get your number,
sentences.zh: 你一进超市就跑到熟食柜台取号，

sentences.en: and then you start walking around and doing the regular shopping,
sentences.zh: 然后开始四处走动，进行正常的购物，

sentences.en: and you watch how the numbers go drop down.
sentences.zh: 你看着号码牌上的数字不断跳动。

sentences.en: And then as soon as it gets close to yours, then you go back.
sentences.zh: 等快到你的号码时，你再回去。

sentences.en: So that's a Q that's been avoided because it's a Q within a Q.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个被规避掉的队列，因为它是一个队列中的队列。

sentences.en: So I have little, little ideas like this.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一些这样的小点子。

sentences.en: Dr. Q hates waiting in line as much as you and I do.
sentences.zh: Q 博士和你我一样讨厌排队。

sentences.en: But he does respect the well-designed Q.
sentences.zh: 但他尊重设计良好的队列。

sentences.en: The Machiavellian experts of Q design are people at Disney World and the Disney properties.
sentences.zh: 队列设计的马基雅维利式专家是迪士尼乐园和迪士尼旗下产业的人。

sentences.en: They have mastered the idea that people can be happy waiting 40 minutes in line for a four-minute ride.
sentences.zh: 他们掌握了一个精髓：人们可以为了一个四分钟的游乐项目而乐于排队 40 分钟。

sentences.en: I think it's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太棒了。

sentences.en: Disney is very serious about Q design.
sentences.zh: 迪士尼对队列设计非常认真。

sentences.en: They employ about 18 or so operations researchers.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣了大约 18 名左右的运筹学研究人员。

sentences.en: They call them imagineers.
sentences.zh: 他们称他们为“幻想工程师”。

sentences.en: These imagineers have mastered the golden rules of Q design.
sentences.zh: 这些幻想工程师掌握了队列设计的黄金法则。

sentences.en: The first is to keep your customers entertained while they wait in line.
sentences.zh: 第一条是让顾客在排队时保持娱乐。

sentences.en: Their guests think that the amusement has started before they actually sit on the ride.
sentences.zh: 他们的游客会认为，在真正坐上游乐设施之前，娱乐就已经开始了。

sentences.en: They'll have video screens along the Q route with games.
sentences.zh: 他们会在队列沿途设置带有游戏的视频屏幕。

sentences.en: And if the lines are getting really ugly, a park manager will send in a sweaty man in a full-body costume.
sentences.zh: 如果排队情况变得非常糟糕，公园经理会派出一个穿着全身玩偶服、满头大汗的人过去。

sentences.en: And so they're entertained and they're amused while they're waiting in line.
sentences.zh: 这样他们在排队时就能得到娱乐和消遣。

sentences.en: The second rule, manage expectations.
sentences.zh: 第二条规则，管理预期。

sentences.en: Always manage your expectations such that you'll deliver above the performance you say.
sentences.zh: 永远管理好你的预期，这样你交付的结果就会高于你所承诺的表现。

sentences.en: So, for instance, if the line says you can anticipate 45-minute wait if the line is out to this point,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果队列显示如果排到这个位置预计需要等待 45 分钟，

sentences.en: when really it might be only 35 minutes.
sentences.zh: 而实际上可能只需要 35 分钟。

sentences.en: So, therefore, if you look at your watch, in 35 minutes you're getting on the line,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你看一眼手表，35 分钟后你就能排到了，

sentences.en: and the dad and the mom and the two kids say, hey, we're 10 minutes ahead of schedule.
sentences.zh: 爸爸妈妈和两个孩子会说，嘿，我们比预定时间提前了 10 分钟。

sentences.en: So that's great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: You waited 35 minutes and you say, we just saved 10 minutes because we thought we're going to have to wait for 45 minutes.
sentences.zh: 你等了 35 分钟，然后说，我们刚刚节省了 10 分钟，因为我们以为要等 45 分钟。

sentences.en: Q theory is about 100 years old now, but it wasn't until the 1950s that the profession really came into its own.
sentences.zh: 队列理论现在大约有 100 年的历史了，但直到 20 世纪 50 年代，这一职业才真正成熟起来。

sentences.en: After World War II, there was a burst of economic activity, a lot more high-rise buildings, high-rise hotels and offices.
sentences.zh: 二战后，经济活动激增，出现了更多的高层建筑、高层酒店和写字楼。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, owners of these buildings were getting complaints about rush-hour delays for elevators.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这些建筑的业主开始收到关于高峰时段电梯延误的投诉。

sentences.en: In those days, of course, they didn't have microprocessors to optimize the movement of the elevators.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，他们当然没有微处理器来优化电梯的运行。

sentences.en: Many of the elevators actually had humans as operators, as pilots, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 许多电梯实际上是有专人操作的，可以说是有“飞行员”的。

sentences.en: So Russ Acoff, who was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 所以，宾夕法尼亚大学的教授拉斯·阿科夫，

sentences.en: sent one of his research aides to New York City to check out these complaints about elevator delays.
sentences.zh: 派了他的一名研究助理去纽约市调查这些关于电梯延误的投诉。

sentences.en: And, indeed, he found out that there were rush hours for elevators.
sentences.zh: 确实，他发现电梯存在高峰时段。

sentences.en: It's like 8 to 9 in the morning or 5 to 6 at night, just like rush hour for cars.
sentences.zh: 就像早上 8 点到 9 点或晚上 5 点到 6 点，就像汽车的交通高峰期一样。

sentences.en: So he said, hmm, the traditional engineering approach,
sentences.zh: 于是他说，嗯，传统的工程方法是，

sentences.en: dynamite this building and start over again with twice as many elevator shafts
sentences.zh: 炸掉这栋楼，重新建造两倍数量的电梯井，

sentences.en: because you've got more demand than you have capacity at these rush hours.
sentences.zh: 因为在这些高峰时段，需求超过了容量。

sentences.en: In my experience, engineers are a lot more crafty than that, but let's just go with it.
sentences.zh: 以我的经验来看，工程师们比这狡猾得多，但我们姑且这么说吧。

sentences.en: But then, in a stroke of genius, he said, well, maybe the problem is framed the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 但随后，他灵机一动，说，也许这个问题被错误地定义了。

sentences.en: Maybe the problem isn't the 90 seconds of wait for the elevators.
sentences.zh: 也许问题不在于电梯 90 秒的等待时间。

sentences.en: Maybe the problem is the complaints about the 90-second waits for the elevators.
sentences.zh: 也许问题在于人们对电梯 90 秒等待时间的投诉。

sentences.en: And if we could reduce the complaints substantially, maybe we'll solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能大幅减少投诉，也许就能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And then, in another stroke of genius, he said, well, what if you give somebody a distraction, a diversion?
sentences.zh: 接着，他又灵机一动，说，如果给人们一些消遣或转移注意力的方法会怎样？

sentences.en: Let's try floor-to-ceiling mirrors next to all the elevators in an experimental building.
sentences.zh: 让我们在一栋实验楼的所有电梯旁尝试安装落地镜。

sentences.en: So you got the money, put the mirrors in, watched for a month, and guess what?
sentences.zh: 于是你有了钱，装上了镜子，观察了一个月，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: The complaints dropped to near zero.
sentences.zh: 投诉几乎降到了零。

sentences.en: Men who were wearing ties could adjust their ties.
sentences.zh: 打领带的男士可以整理领带。

sentences.en: Women could make sure their hair was organized okay.
sentences.zh: 女士们可以确保她们的发型没问题。

sentences.en: Or vice versa.
sentences.zh: 反之亦然。

sentences.en: Sometimes men and women were even seen to flirt occasionally through the reflection.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至能看到男女通过倒影偶尔调情。

sentences.en: I guess it's less provocative than eye-to-eye contact.
sentences.zh: 我想这比眼神交流的挑逗性要小一些。

sentences.en: The complaints dropped to near zero.
sentences.zh: 投诉几乎降到了零。

sentences.en: Problem solved.
sentences.zh: 问题解决了。

sentences.en: The statistics of the delay unchanged.
sentences.zh: 延误的统计数据没有改变。

sentences.en: Ingenious.
sentences.zh: 天才。

sentences.en: Mirrors won't work at McDonald's or Whole Foods, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，镜子在麦当劳或全食超市可不管用。

sentences.en: Many fast food restaurants and most grocery stores use parallel queues,
sentences.zh: 许多快餐店和大多数杂货店使用平行队列，

sentences.en: where there's a bunch of open lanes and you're forced to pick one and stick with it.
sentences.zh: 那里有一堆开放的通道，你被迫选择一个并坚持下去。

sentences.en: The one next to you could be going faster for any number of reasons,
sentences.zh: 你旁边的那条队可能因为各种原因走得更快，

sentences.en: and it's totally frustrating, but you stay in your line, and you play the hand you're dealt.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人沮丧，但你只能留在自己的队伍里，接受你所面对的局面。

sentences.en: But there's another way to do it.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一种方法。

sentences.en: A single serpentine line that feeds all of the open registers.
sentences.zh: 一条单一的蛇形队列，通向所有开放的收银台。

sentences.en: It's first come, first served.
sentences.zh: 这是先到先得。

sentences.en: It's a cue designed for equality and fairness.
sentences.zh: 这是一个为平等和公平而设计的队列。

sentences.en: And when there's one line, both blatant and inadvertent cue jumping is minimized.
sentences.zh: 当只有一条队列时，无论是明目张胆还是无意间的插队行为都会降到最低。

sentences.en: We call them slips and skips.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“slips”（溜号）和“skips”（跳号）。

sentences.en: In American companies, they used to pride themselves on designing these more egalitarian cues.
sentences.zh: 在美国公司，他们过去以设计这些更平等的队列而自豪。

sentences.en: Wendy's is very proud that they're the first ones in fast food that had the single serpentine line.
sentences.zh: 温蒂汉堡非常自豪他们是快餐业中第一个采用单一蛇形队列的。

sentences.en: American Airlines is very proud.
sentences.zh: 美国航空也非常自豪。

sentences.en: They claim that they're the first ones that have single serpentine line in airports,
sentences.zh: 他们声称自己是机场中第一个采用单一蛇形队列的，

sentences.en: although British Air argues with them.
sentences.zh: 尽管英国航空对此有异议。

sentences.en: They say, well, they got it at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，他们是同时采用的。

sentences.en: There used to be a bank in New York called Chemical Bank,
sentences.zh: 纽约曾有一家银行叫化学银行，

sentences.en: and they used to claim that they were the first ones to have that in their bank lobbies.
sentences.zh: 他们过去常声称自己是银行大厅里第一个采用这种队列的。

sentences.en: And so there's a certain pride to getting rid of inadvertent line jumping by slips and skips
sentences.zh: 因此，通过单一蛇形队列来消除无意间的插队行为，确实有一种自豪感。

sentences.en: by having the single serpentine line.
sentences.zh: 但今天，队列设计正在发生变化。

sentences.en: But today, cue design is changing.
sentences.zh: 我们越来越多地遇到这样设计的队列，以便为不同群体提供不同级别的服务。

sentences.en: More and more, we're encountering cues that are designed so that different levels of service
sentences.zh: 优先队列，以及给予某些人优于他人的优先权。

sentences.en: can be provided to different groups of people.
sentences.zh: 你可以在迪士尼这样的游乐场所看到这一点。

sentences.en: Priority cues and giving certain people priorities over others.
sentences.zh: 但更严重的是，它发生在一些生死攸关的情况下，

sentences.en: You can see it in amusements like Disney.
sentences.zh: 比如器官捐献移植的排队。

sentences.en: But more seriously, it occurs in some life-and-death situations,
sentences.zh: 我的假设是，这种设计变化与队列愤怒有关，

sentences.en: like cueing for organ donation transplants.
sentences.zh: 这种现象正变得越来越普遍，而且可以在 YouTube 上免费观看。

sentences.en: My hypothesis is that this design change is connected to the cue rage
sentences.zh: 我也相信，理解这种新的队列理论将有助于我们更好地理解

sentences.en: that's becoming more and more commonplace and available to watch for free on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 这个国家日益增长的不平等和差距。

sentences.en: And I also believe that understanding this new cue theory will better help us understand
sentences.zh: 是的，你可能会说，为什么拥有大量飞行里程的人

sentences.en: the inequality and disparity that's on the rise in this country.
sentences.zh: 应该自动升到头等舱，

sentences.en: Yeah, you might say, well, why should somebody with a lot of frequent flyer mileage
sentences.zh: 正如我最近在一些航班上发现的那样，

sentences.en: get automatically bumped up to first class,
sentences.zh: 从而可以避开机场的 TSA 安检队列。

sentences.en: as I found out I recently was on some flights,
sentences.zh: 对此我感到有点内疚。

sentences.en: and therefore then can escape the TSA queue in airports.
sentences.zh: 就在昨天，我做了两次。

sentences.en: And I feel a little bit guilty about that.
sentences.zh: 我感到有点内疚，因为队伍里有大约 30 个人，

sentences.en: And just yesterday, I did this twice.
sentences.zh: 而我直接走到了最前面。

sentences.en: And I felt a little bit guilty because there were like 30 people in line,
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯，这公平吗？

sentences.en: and I went right to the front of it.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我比别人飞得多一点。

sentences.en: And I thought, hmm, why is this fair?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你的问题是一个深刻的问题，

sentences.en: Just because I fly a little bit more than the others do.
sentences.zh: 需要更多的思考和讨论。

sentences.en: And so I think your question is a deep one
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由本杰明·沃克和我，罗曼·马尔斯制作。

sentences.en: and requires some more thought and discussion.
sentences.zh: 我还需要再跟你介绍一遍本杰明·沃克吗？

sentences.zh: 来自 WFMU 的过多信息。
